keep: The idea is named up front: linked rates are a matrix times the amounts, x′ = Ax, and measured along A's eigenvectors each part changes on its own, so the motion is their sum.

The picture is the brief's state plane: the real system on the left (open tanks A = [−0.2 0.05; 0.2 −0.2], closed tanks, two masses on three springs), one dot (x₁, x₂) on the right with the eigenvector lines labelled, a draggable start and Go, two faint dots riding the lines with the real dot their sum, and the middle spring's stretch reading 0 for a together start.

One worked example runs from the rule with real numbers: A from the flows, eigenvalues −0.1 with (1, 2) and −0.3 with (1, −2) checked by trace and determinant, 30 g split as 15 of each, x₂ = 30e^(−0.1t) − 30e^(−0.3t), the peak of about 11.5 g at 5 ln 3 ≈ 5.49 minutes when the tanks match, and the 1 : 2 share at 30 minutes. The masses use lesson 5's B = [2 −1; −1 2] with k/m = 100, giving 10 and about 17.3 rad/s.

The brief's misconceptions each get a DO screen with its own hint: the tank sign slip (2), each e^(λt) paired with its own eigenvector (6), ω taken as the eigenvalue (10), and the start's numbers read as mode amounts (12). The decoupled equation seen as the decay rule is screen 5's faint dots.

Thirteen screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11) and DO (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), ending with two mixed puzzles (12, 13). Three footnotes, each on a result he might look up, none naming a source. The two rooms sharing a wall is a new analogy with the same average and difference modes, and it says where it breaks.
fix: Causal step skipped for the masses: 'work the same way' does not say why their equations come apart. Say that along an eigenvector B only stretches, so each amount obeys a″ = −(k/m)λa, the spring rule from differential equations.

Causal step skipped for the opposite swing: 'the middle spring pulls too, so it is faster' leaves out how much. The middle spring stretches by twice each mass's shift, so each mass feels k from its outer spring and 2k from the middle one, 3k in all.
Causal step skipped on the state plane: 'start on a line and it runs straight along it' needs its reason in explain. The other amount starts at zero, and zero times e^(λt) stays zero.
False absolute: 'With e^(λt), the larger eigenvalue takes over' needs 'as long as the start has some of it', as practice says.
Overstated in practice: 'Mixing tanks, heat passing between rooms and masses on springs all work this way' holds for their linear models only. Say they can all be written this way.
Muddled number: screen 10 calls 300 'its eigenvalue' while screen 9 says B's eigenvalue is 3. Say the eigenvalue of (k/m)B is 3k/m = 300, and that is ω².

Phone layout and picture wording: say the real thing sits above the state plane on a phone; screen 11's trail fills a diamond-shaped box, not just 'a box'; the tank drag wording 'less than no salt' is clumsy there; and each idea screen's words should be held to about 90 words.
Misconception shown failing in explain: add one sentence that 300 rad/s, the eigenvalue itself, is the slip, since ω is its square root.
